thread:
sasha: Heads-up — since ~03:10 UTC we're seeing a pile of GPU provisioning failures in us-west1. Root cause looks like local scratch attach failing with ENOSPC on the node. Error in autoscaler logs: "attach failed: no free local nvme".
chen: saw that alert. I pulled node metrics — ephemeral free bytes dropped from ~45GB to <2GB in a few minutes, and iops on the reclaimer process spiked.
sasha: same. Wondering if the recent janitor config change that increased reclaim aggressiveness overshot. We bumped target_free_pct from 5 -> 15 last night.
devon: that change was intended to reduce eviction churn for long jobs by freeing more headroom. But looks like reclaimer went into full-scan mode and started mass-evictions which saturated local IO. Reclaimer iops went from ~180/s to ~1200/s per disk.
opsbot: deploy-bot: config-change deploy completed by devex at 3101233300 to cluster-janitor (target_free_pct=15).
chen: logs from one affected node: ```
[2026-04-03T03:12:24Z] reclaimer: evicting 42 containers
[2026-04-03T03:12:24Z] nvme0n1: write latency spiked to 35ms
[2026-04-03T03:12:26Z] kworker: I/O error - WRITE failed (ENOSPC)
```
sasha: that IO spike caused kubelet attach to time out when creating scratch volumes for new GPU pods. So provisioner kept retrying -> backlog.
irene: quick question: is this isolated to us-west1?
chen: so far predominantly us-west1 and one node pool in eu-west3 that shares the same janitor config. other regions have lower traffic and the reclaimer stays calm.
devon: hypothesis: reclaim sweep is single-threaded but throttles poorly when it hits many small files. The sweep logic issues many small deletes which produces write amplification on NVMe -> wear + iops.
sasha: we need a mitigation ASAP because customer-facing jobs are stuck. Proposed short-term: roll back target_free_pct to 7 and throttle reclaimer concurrency to 4, disable full-scan for 30m. Also pause any large batch deployments for 1 hour.
leo: +1 on rollback. Can we also temporarily mark one extra gnode pool as burst-capacity with larger scratch (temp attach of network-backed volume) as a fallback for provisioning? That costs more but unblocks customers.
devon: we can spin up network-backed scratchclass for new pods with a feature-flag, yes. Quick estimate: ~40 nodes x $0.12/hr extra -> ~ $115/day.
opsbot: incident-bot: incident created #INC-2026-3141 (local-nvme-reclaim-surge).
chen: I'm toggling the feature flag to reduce reclaim target now (doing canary in us-west1-a first). I'll post when done.
chen: toggled — target_free_pct back to 7 in us-west1-a at 3101234402. Reclaimer concurrency set to 4.
sasha: seeing immediate drop in reclaimer iops on canary nodes. Free space trending up. Provisioning retries are clearing.
leo: I'll approve a temporary burst pool for next 6 hours. Devex please add cost note to the incident ticket.
devon: follow-up: need longer-term fixes — change reclaimer to batch deletes in larger transactions, add backoff when NVMe latency > 10ms, and add a safety throttle when provisioner backlog > 50 pods. I'll open PRs.
irene: can we also add a metric and alert for sudden reclaim iops surge? Current alert only watches free bytes.
chen: good call — adding reclaim_iops and nvme_write_latency alerts.
sasha: action items: 1) rollback full config in us-west1 (done canary, rolling), 2) enable burst network scratch pool (leo/dl), 3) devon to send PR for reclaimer batching + latency backoff, 4) chen add reclaim_iops alert, 5) ops to update runbook with rollback steps.
leo: I'll own the burst pool. devon — ping me on PR, will review.
devon: will file PRs and test in staging; aiming for a safer reclaimer in 48h.
chen: closing loop: us-west1 provisioning error rate down to baseline, attaching queues drained. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours then close incident. :thumbsup:
sasha: thanks all. Update the incident ticket with postmortem notes and cost delta.
